parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Maple Ridge · Silver Valley, Yennadon and the north

North Maple Ridge is a sub-area name used in the MLS®, and the City of Maple Ridge has no published boundary for it. Looking at the City’s neighbourhood list, you will find Yennadon, Whonnock, Webster’s Corners, Town Centre, Thornhill, Silver Valley, Ruskin, Port Haney, Port Hammond and Albion/Kanaka, but no north area.

As a rough guide only, I think of it as roughly 224 Street to 240 Street, north of Dewdney Trunk Road and the Town Centre, up to and across the Alouette River into Silver Valley. That is my reading from the addresses below, not a City boundary, and it overlaps my

. The closest official descriptions are Silver Valley, which the City says is on the north side of the Alouette River and is a gateway to popular recreation areas, and Yennadon, which the City calls an active agricultural production area and a major recreation centre.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 17, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Maple Ridge and School District 42.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations, flood rules and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for North Maple Ridge

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The City adopted the Silver Valley Area Plan update on November 25, 2025. It is Section 10.3 of the Official Community Plan.

According to the City, in 2025 it adopted updates to its Official Community Plan as well as the area plans for Town Centre, Hammond, Silver Valley and Albion. The Albion plan was adopted on October 28, while the rest followed in November.

The Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan was adopted by the City on January 27, 2026 under Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021. Its area follows Lougheed Highway between Maple Meadows Way and 221 Street.

ALR: I did not find an official statement placing Agricultural Land Reserve land inside North Maple Ridge as a whole. ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the Agricultural Land Commission map.

The City’s Official Community Plan includes policies to enhance and promote farming on lands designated in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and the City describes Yennadon as an active agricultural production area.

Two floodplain maps are published by the City: one for the North and South Alouette River and one for the Fraser River. A floodplain map, the City says, outlines the area expected to flood once every 200 years on average.
Rainfall and water levels on Kanaka Creek, the Fraser River and the North and South Alouette River are monitored by the City.
Landslides and debris flows are a risk in some parts of Maple Ridge, the City says, and it adds that snowpack melt during warm weather can set off landslides.
I found no flood or slope area named for North Maple Ridge as a whole, so check the City’s maps for the exact address.

Maple Ridge has two West Coast Express stops, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station. There are five trips a day, Monday to Friday: they leave Maple Ridge in the morning and come back in the evening.

The Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit line proposed by TransLink would be 22 km long, with 13 stations and a bus every 10 minutes at peak. It is in detailed planning, TransLink says, and has preliminary funding from the 2025 Investment Plan, but more funding is needed to build it.

How do I get around from North Maple Ridge?
Route 733 links Rock Ridge Drive at 133 Avenue to Haney Place, following 232 Street up from Dewdney Trunk Road. Port Haney Station is the end or the start of some weekday trips.

Route 741 serves Anderson Creek Drive at 232 Street and Haney Place. Heading out it takes 227 Street, then 128 Avenue and 232 Street, followed by 136 Avenue and 137 Avenue. On the return it takes 141 Avenue and Silver Valley Road. A number of weekday trips start from or continue on to Port Haney Station.

Riders can use either of the two Maple Ridge stops on the West Coast Express, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station. Five trips run each weekday, heading out in the morning and coming back in the evening.

Timetable dates: 733, effective June 23, 2025; 741, effective April 20, 2026. TransLink’s August 24, 2026 news post says service improvements on routes 733 and 741 start September 7, 2026, so check the current timetable.
Which schools are in North Maple Ridge?

The Province’s school list shows Yennadon Elementary at 23347 128 Avenue, Kanaka Creek Elementary at 11120 234A Street, Alexander Robinson Elementary at 11849 238B Street, Harry Hooge Elementary at 12280 230 Street, Golden Ears Elementary at 23124 118 Avenue, Maple Ridge Secondary at 21911 122 Avenue and Thomas Haney Secondary at 23000 116 Avenue.
Catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with
What parks and library are there?
Maple Ridge Park is at 13180 232 Street, on the South Alouette River.
Golden Ears Provincial Park is 11 km north of Maple Ridge, reached by Dewdney Trunk Road, 232nd Street and Fern Crescent.
Maple Ridge’s only Fraser Valley Regional Library branch is the Maple Ridge Public Library, at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road.
What plan covers North Maple Ridge?
The Silver Valley Area Plan, Section 10.3 of the Official Community Plan, was updated on November 25, 2025, and the City’s Town Centre plan was updated in November 2025.
I found no plan written for North Maple Ridge as a whole.
Is North Maple Ridge in a floodplain or on a slope?

The City’s floodplain maps for Maple Ridge cover the North and South Alouette River and the Fraser River. A floodplain map, as the City describes it, outlines the area expected to flood once in every 200 years on average.
According to the City, parts of Maple Ridge can see landslides and debris flows, and warm weather that melts the snowpack can bring landslides on as well.
